questions.scenario: During the construction of a reinforced concrete basement wall, the RGBC's quality control team discovers that an 8-metre section was cast using an unapproved concrete mix with compressive strength 40% below the design specified on approved plans. The Authorized Person (AP) advises the RGBC to apply carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) strengthening quietly without disturbing the Buildings Department. What is the statutory obligation of the RGBC Authorized Signatory under Section 9(5)(b) of the Buildings Ordinance?
options: A. Accede to the AP's instruction, as the AP holds ultimate statutory design responsibility under Section 4.
B. Submit a retrospective minor works notification to the Building Authority once the CFRP strengthening design is ready.
C. Give immediate written notice to the Building Authority of the material defect and divergence, irrespective of the AP's instructions.
D. Apply to the Building Authority for a modification of the Building (Construction) Regulations under Section 42 before continuing basement works.
questions.rationale: Under BO Section 9(5)(b), a registered general building contractor must give written notice to the Building Authority if it comes to their knowledge that any building works have been or are being carried out in contravention of the Ordinance or diverge in a material manner from approved plans, or that any material defect has occurred. This is an independent statutory duty on the contractor that cannot be overridden or waived by the AP. Failure to report constitutes an offense under Section 40(2A).

questions.scenario: An RGBC obtained consent from the Building Authority to commence site formation works on 15 January. After carrying out bulk excavation for four weeks, works were fully halted on 12 February due to an unforeseen commercial dispute. The site remains completely idle until 20 May (over 3 months of continuous suspension). The dispute is resolved and the RGBC wishes to re-mobilize and resume excavation immediately. What is the statutory status of the consent under Section 20?
options: A. The consent remains valid because it had already been acted upon within the initial 3-month window from the consent date.
B. The consent is deemed to be revoked under Section 20(1) because works were suspended for 3 months; the RGBC cannot resume works without an application for renewal via Form BA9.
C. The consent automatically extends for another 28 days upon notifying the Building Authority in writing under B(A)R Regulation 20.
D. The consent is unaffected, but the Authorized Signatory must submit an updated Site Safety Supervision Plan before work resumes.
questions.rationale: Under Section 20(1) of the Buildings Ordinance, if building works for which consent has been given are not commenced within 3 months, OR if commenced are suspended for a period of 3 months, the consent is deemed to be revoked. Under Section 20(2) and B(A)R Regulation 34, a renewal application must be submitted (Form BA9) and approved prior to resumption. Carrying out works after deemed revocation is an offense under Section 14(1) and Section 40(1A).

questions.scenario: A consent for the construction of large-diameter bored piles includes a statutory condition imposed by the Building Authority under Section 17(1) requiring pre-grouting core verification and post-installation proof drilling to a depth of 5 metres into sound bedrock. Due to project delay, the RGBC AS agrees with the RSE to drill only 2 metres into bedrock where good rock recovery was observed in adjacent boreholes. What statutory consequence applies to the RGBC under the Buildings Ordinance?
options: A. It is legally permissible provided the RSE certifies in the pile installation record that 2 metres penetration is structurally sufficient.
B. The RGBC AS is liable to criminal prosecution under Section 40(2AA) for failing to comply with a condition imposed by the Building Authority under Section 17(1).
C. The condition can be varied administratively by notifying the BD Chief Structural Engineer within 14 days of completion of the pile.
D. No offense is committed unless the bored pile suffers settlement exceeding the allowable threshold during proof load testing.
questions.rationale: Under Section 17(1) of the Buildings Ordinance, the Building Authority may impose conditions on consents, including verification drilling. Compliance with these conditions is mandatory. Under Section 40(2AA), any person who fails to comply with any condition imposed under Section 17(1) commits a criminal offense liable to a fine of $250,000 and 6 months' imprisonment. Neither the RSE nor the RGBC has the legal power to relax Section 17 conditions unilaterally.

questions.scenario: An RGBC completes the superstructure of a commercial development, and the AP applies to the Building Authority for an Occupation Permit (OP) under Section 21. Upon joint inspection, the BD officer finds that the foul water drainage system has not been connected to the public sewerage system as shown on approved plans, but rather discharges into a temporary retention sump. How does Section 21(6) govern the Building Authority's determination?
options: A. The Building Authority may grant a Temporary Occupation Permit (TOP) for 12 months provided the RGBC posts a cash bond.
B. The Building Authority must refuse to issue an Occupation Permit under Section 21(6)(d) because the drainage works have not been completed in accordance with the approved plans and regulations.
C. The Building Authority must issue the Occupation Permit but serve a statutory warning letter giving 28 days to complete the connection.
D. The Building Authority has no jurisdiction over drainage outfalls if the Environmental Protection Department has issued a discharge license.
questions.rationale: Section 21(6)(d) of the Buildings Ordinance provides that the Building Authority shall refuse to issue an Occupation Permit or Temporary Occupation Permit if it appears that any drainage works have not been completed in accordance with the regulations and approved plans. The connection to the public sewerage system is a fundamental prerequisite for OP issuance under Cap. 123.

questions.scenario: During the erection of external scaffolding for high-rise facade cladding, an RGBC fails to install catch-fans and protective safety netting above an active ground-level bus terminus. BD officers perform an emergency site audit, observe debris falling onto the pavement, and immediately serve a Cease Works Order on the RGBC. Which statutory section empowers this order and what is the legal effect?
options: A. Section 24, requiring demolition of the scaffolding within 21 days.
B. Section 24A, requiring immediate closure of the bus terminus under a District Court warrant.
C. Section 23, empowering the Building Authority to order the immediate cessation of building works carried out in a dangerous manner.
D. Section 13, initiating instantaneous disciplinary proceedings against the RGBC's Authorized Signatory.
questions.rationale: Section 23 of the Buildings Ordinance empowers the Building Authority to issue a Cease Works Order where building works are being carried out in such a manner as to cause, or to be likely to cause, a risk of injury to any person or damage to any property. The order takes effect immediately upon service. Continuing works after such an order is a serious criminal offense under Section 40(2D).

questions.scenario: An RGBC carrying out trench excavation along an alleyway induces severe ground loss, causing adjacent pre-war unreinforced masonry dwellings to exhibit rapid, gaping structural fractures. BD structural engineers assess that the dwellings are liable to imminent collapse. To safeguard life, the Building Authority applies to the District Court for an emergency order to bar access and evict the occupants. Under which statutory provision is this application made?
options: A. Section 24(1) - Demolition Order for unauthorized structures.
B. Section 24A - Closure Order for buildings rendered dangerous or liable to become dangerous.
C. Section 27 - Notice requiring full shoring and underpinning.
D. Section 23 - Cease Works Order against the affected building occupants.
questions.rationale: Under Section 24A of the Buildings Ordinance, the District Court may, upon application by the Building Authority, make a Closure Order to close any building that is dangerous or liable to become dangerous, preventing all non-authorized entry until it is made safe. Section 24 is for removal of unauthorized building works, whereas Section 24A specifically provides the statutory machinery for evacuating and closing dangerous premises.

questions.scenario: When applying for the completion of structural alteration works under Form BA14, the RGBC Authorized Signatory knowingly submits false material testing laboratory certificates showing compliant carbonation and chloride depth tests for existing concrete cores, when in fact no such tests were conducted. What criminal offense has been committed by the AS under Cap. 123?
options: A. An offense under Section 40(1A) for carrying out building works without prior approval.
B. An offense under Section 40(1AA) for knowingly misrepresenting a material fact in a document submitted to the Building Authority.
C. An offense under Section 40(2) for failing to give statutory notice to the Commissioner for Labour.
D. An administrative non-compliance under PNRC 38 without statutory criminal liability under the primary ordinance.
questions.rationale: Section 40(1AA) of the Buildings Ordinance creates an express criminal offense where any person knowingly misrepresents any material fact or makes any false statement in any plan, certificate, form, report, notice or other document given to the Building Authority. A convicted offender is liable to a fine of $500,000 and imprisonment for 3 years.

questions.scenario: To accelerate slab cycle times on a multi-storey project, an RGBC removes temporary backpropping from transfer beams across three floors below a freshly cast slab, directly contrary to the approved construction sequence and structural calculations. Although the transfer beams defuse excessive deflection and large shear cracks form, the structure does not collapse and nobody is hurt. Under what provision is the RGBC and its AS criminally liable?
options: A. Section 40(2B)(b) for carrying out building works in a manner likely to cause a risk of injury to any person or damage to any property.
B. Section 40(6) only, because no physical collapse or personal injury occurred.
C. Section 40(1), which is restricted to minor regulatory fines not exceeding $5,000.
D. No criminal liability arises under Cap. 123 unless a formal Cease Works Order has been issued by the BD and defied.
questions.rationale: Under Section 40(2B)(b), any person who directly or indirectly carries out or causes to be carried out building works in such a manner as to cause or to be likely to cause a risk of injury to any person or damage to any property is guilty of an offense. Actual collapse or injury is NOT a prerequisite; creating the risk is the gravamen of the offense, carrying a maximum penalty of a $1,000,000 fine and 3 years' imprisonment.

questions.scenario: An RGBC is convicted in the Magistrates' Court under Section 40(2A) for material divergence from approved plans during structural steel roof erection. Following criminal conviction, the Building Authority refers the contractor to a Disciplinary Board under Section 13. Which of the following combinations of orders is strictly within the statutory powers of the Disciplinary Board under Section 13(4)?
options: A. Ordering removal of the contractor from the register and sentencing the Authorized Signatory to 6 months' suspended imprisonment.
B. Imposing a criminal fine of $500,000 and revoking the building's Occupation Permit.
C. Ordering that the contractor be removed from the register permanently or for a specified period, reprimanding them, and ordering a fine not exceeding $250,000.
D. Ordering the immediate demolition of the structural steel roof without right of appeal to the Building Appeals Tribunal.
questions.rationale: Under Section 13(4) and (4A) of the Buildings Ordinance, a Disciplinary Board has quasi-judicial administrative powers to: (a) order removal from the register (permanent or fixed term), (b) order a reprimand, (c) order payment of a fine not exceeding $250,000, and (d) order the payment of inquiry costs. A Disciplinary Board has NO statutory power to impose custodial sentences (which lie solely with criminal courts) nor issue demolition orders.

questions.scenario: An RGBC AS procures structural Grade 500B reinforcing steel bars from an uncertified overseas mill lacking BD Quality Assurance Scheme recognition. Subsequent laboratory tensile tests demonstrate that the yield strength is deficient by 25%. However, the contractor embeds the steel in columns and conceals it with formwork before the AP/RSE can inspect it. What statutory duty under Section 9(5)(c) has been violated, and what criminal liability is triggered?
options: A. Breach of duty to supervise; punishable only through an administrative letter from the BD Quality Management Unit.
B. Breach of duty under Section 9(5)(c) to use materials that are suitable, free from defects, and compliant with regulations; punishable under Section 40(2A)(c).
C. Breach of duty under B(A)R Regulation 11; punishable by a maximum fine of $2,000 under the general summary offenses provisions.
D. No offense under Cap. 123 provided the concrete wrap provides a minimum 40mm cover.
questions.rationale: Section 9(5)(c) of the Buildings Ordinance statutorily requires a registered contractor to use such materials as are suitable for the purpose, free from defects, and comply with the regulations. Under Section 40(2A)(c), any registered contractor who fails to comply with Section 9(5)(c) commits an offense liable to a fine of $1,000,000 and imprisonment for 3 years.

questions.scenario: A developer terminates the existing main contractor during the superstructure construction of a 30-storey hotel and formally selects a new RGBC to take over the project. Before the new RGBC can validly enter the site and proceed with any structural building operations, which statutory notification sequence must be strictly fulfilled under the Building (Administration) Regulations?
options: A. The developer must submit Form BA10 signed only by the new RGBC at least 7 days before physical works resume on site.
B. The building owner must notify the Building Authority of the appointment of the new RGBC on specified Form BA8, accompanied by the new RGBC's formal acceptance.
C. The new RGBC must submit Form BA14 certifying practical completion of all structural works executed up to the handover date.
D. The Authorized Person must apply for a completely new Building Authority plan approval under Section 14(1) of the Buildings Ordinance before appointing the new RGBC.
questions.rationale: Under Building (Administration) Regulation 8, both the person for whom building works are carried out (owner/developer) and the contractor must notify the Building Authority of any change/appointment of a registered general building contractor on the specified Form BA8. Resuming site operations without filing Form BA8 constitutes an offense under Cap. 123. Form BA10 is the notice of commencement (not appointment), Form BA14 is for completion of works, and re-approval of plans under s.14(1) is not required solely due to a change of contractor.

questions.scenario: An RGBC obtained consent under Section 16(1)(b) of the Buildings Ordinance to carry out deep basement excavation works on 1 March 2024. Due to protracted machinery mobilization and supply chain delays, no physical works commenced on site, and three months have elapsed since the consent was granted.
options: A. The consent remains valid automatically for 12 months provided the Authorized Signatory submits a monthly progress affidavit to the Building Authority.
B. The consent is deemed revoked under Section 20(1) of the Buildings Ordinance, and an application for renewal of consent on Form BA9 must be submitted and approved before any works commence.
C. The RGBC can immediately proceed by simply issuing a Form BA10 notice to the Building Authority not less than 48 hours prior to breaking ground.
D. The RGBC must make an application under B(A)R Regulation 27 to obtain a formal 6-month statutory dispensation.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance Section 20(1) & (2), B(A)R Regulation 34, Form BA9
questions.rationale: Under Section 20(1) of the Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123), a consent to commence building works is deemed to be revoked if the works are not commenced within 3 months of the date of the consent. To resume or begin works, an application for renewal of consent must be made under Section 20(2) on specified Form BA9 pursuant to B(A)R Regulation 34. (Note: B(A)R Regulation 27 has been repealed; relying on Regulation 27 is obsolete, and Form BA10 cannot cure a revoked consent).

questions.scenario: An RGBC holds an active consent to construct a private hospital superstructure. The project team intends to commence the first structural pour on Tuesday, 18 June. What is the statutory deadline for submitting the formal notice of commencement (Form BA10) to the Building Authority pursuant to the Building (Administration) Regulations?
options: A. Not less than 7 days before the commencement date, meaning the BA10 must be received by the Building Authority on or before Tuesday, 11 June.
B. Not less than 14 days before the commencement date, meaning the BA10 must be received on or before Tuesday, 4 June.
C. Exactly 24 hours prior to commencing any physical structural work on the site.
D. Concurrently with the submission of the Form BA14 practical completion certificate upon finishing the works.
questions.rationale: Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1) stipulates that a registered contractor must give to the Building Authority not less than 7 days' notice in writing on the specified form (Form BA10) of the date on which building works or street works will be commenced. Submitting less than 7 days in advance or attempting concurrent notice with completion violates B(A)R Reg. 20(1) and exposes the AS and contractor to prosecution under Section 40(2A).

questions.scenario: A new 40-storey residential tower has reached physical completion. The Authorized Person wishes to apply for an Occupation Permit under Section 21 of the Buildings Ordinance using Form BA12/BA13. Before the Building Authority can accept and process this OP application, which document must be duly executed by the RGBC's Authorized Signatory?
options: A. Form MW05 certifying rectification of unauthorized building works.
B. Form BA14 certifying that the building works have been completed in accordance with the Buildings Ordinance and the approved plans.
C. Form BA9 confirming the retrospective extension of the initial consent period.
D. Form BA8 transferring all residual site responsibilities to the property management agency.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulation 25, Form BA14 & Buildings Ordinance Section 21
questions.rationale: Under Building (Administration) Regulation 25 and Section 21 of the Buildings Ordinance, an application for an temporary or full Occupation Permit (Form BA12 or BA13) must be supported by a certificate of completion from the RGBC on specified Form BA14. By signing Form BA14, the RGBC's Authorized Signatory certifies under statutory penalty that the building works have been carried out in accordance with the provisions of Cap. 123 and the approved plans.

questions.scenario: A specialist subcontractor registered as a Registered Specialist Contractor (Ventilation Works Category) completes the installation of designated mechanical ventilation systems in a newly erected commercial complex. For the application for an Occupation Permit, which statutory certification form must be signed and delivered by this RSC?
options: A. Form BA10 (Ventilation)
B. Form BA14A (Certificate of Completion by Registered Specialist Contractor)
C. Form BA11 (Notice of Resumption of Specialist Works)
D. Form MW02 (Class I Ventilation Verification)
questions.rationale: Under Building (Administration) Regulation 25, where specialist works are carried out by a Registered Specialist Contractor (RSC), the completion of such specialized works must be certified on Form BA14A by the Authorized Signatory of the RSC, accompanying or corroborating the RGBC's Form BA14 for the overall project prior to OP issuance.

questions.scenario: A commercial property owner engages an RGBC to carry out Class I Minor Works under the Simplified Requirements of the Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N). To comply strictly with statutory submission procedures, what is the mandatory timing and form requirement for notification prior to commencing these Class I works?
options: A. The RGBC and the Prescribed Building Professional (PBP) must submit specified Form MW01 not less than 7 days before commencement of works.
B. The RGBC alone must submit Form MW05 at least 48 hours prior to commencing any physical operations.
C. The PBP must submit Form MW03 within 14 days after physical works have been completed on site.
D. The RGBC must submit Form BA10 directly to the Central Inspection Team at least 3 days prior to commencement.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Sections 27 & 28, Form MW01
questions.rationale: Under Sections 27 and 28 of the Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N), for Class I minor works, the prescribed building professional (PBP) and registered contractor (RGBC or Registered Minor Works Contractor) must jointly submit the notice of commencement and plan of works on specified Form MW01 to the Building Authority not less than 7 days before the commencement of the works. Form BA10 belongs to conventional consent under B(A)R, whereas MW01 is the statutory instrument under MWCS.

questions.scenario: An RGBC is appointed as the Registered Minor Works Contractor for an alteration project consisting solely of Class II Minor Works under Cap. 123N. No Prescribed Building Professional (PBP) is statutorily required for this specific Class II work item. What is the statutory notification requirement prior to commencement?
options: A. Notice of commencement on Form MW01 must be lodged 14 days in advance.
B. Notice of commencement on specified Form MW03 must be submitted to the Building Authority not less than 7 days before the commencement of the works.
C. No prior notice is required before commencement, provided that Form MW06 is lodged within 14 days of completion.
D. A conventional consent application under Section 14 of the Buildings Ordinance on Form BA8 must be approved.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Section 30 & Form MW03
questions.rationale: Under Section 30 of the Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N), where Class II minor works are to be carried out without a Prescribed Building Professional (PBP), the registered contractor must submit a notice of commencement on specified Form MW03 to the Building Authority not less than 7 days before the works commence. Form MW01 applies to Class I or Class II with a PBP, while Class III requires no prior notice.

questions.scenario: An RGBC completes a Class III Minor Works item (Item 3.1: erection of a standard drying rack conforming to specified dimensions on an external wall) in accordance with Cap. 123N. Which form must be submitted, and what is the strict statutory timeframe for doing so after completion?
options: A. Form MW01 within 7 days prior to starting work.
B. Form MW05 within 14 days after the completion of the works.
C. Form MW02 within 28 days following the end of the calendar month.
D. Form BA14 within 7 days of site demobilization.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Section 35 & Form MW05
questions.rationale: Under Section 35 of the Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N), Class III minor works do not require any prior notification before commencement. However, the registered contractor (RGBC/RMWC) must submit a certificate of completion together with photos/drawings on specified Form MW05 to the Building Authority within 14 days after the completion of the works. Form BA14 is strictly for works under the conventional consent regime.

questions.scenario: A retail tenant commissions an RGBC to carry out Class I minor works involving structural alterations to internal non-load-bearing partitions and above-ceiling HVAC ducting under the supervision of an Authorized Person (PBP). Following physical completion of these Class I works, which document must be certified and lodged with the Building Authority?
options: A. Form MW02 (Certificate of completion of Class I minor works) submitted jointly by the PBP and the RGBC within 14 days after completion.
B. Form BA13 application for a temporary Occupation Permit within 7 days.
C. Form MW04 within 2 months following client final handover.
D. Form MW05 signed solely by the RGBC Authorized Signatory within 48 hours.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Section 29 & Form MW02
questions.rationale: Under Section 29 of Cap. 123N, for Class I minor works, the prescribed building professional (PBP) and the registered contractor must jointly certify completion on specified Form MW02 and submit it to the Building Authority within 14 days after completion of the works, together with as-built record plans and photos. Form MW05 is for Class III works, and Form MW04 is for Class II works with a PBP.

questions.scenario: An RGBC has completed Class II minor works where no Prescribed Building Professional (PBP) was appointed, having properly submitted Form MW03 prior to commencement. Which form must the RGBC submit to certify completion, and what is the statutory time limit?
options: A. Form MW06 within 14 days after the completion of the works.
B. Form MW04 within 7 days before physical occupancy.
C. Form BA14 accompanied by a geotechnical test certificate within 21 days.
D. Form MW05 within 28 days of completing the works.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Section 32 & Form MW06
questions.rationale: Under Section 32 of the Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N), upon completion of Class II minor works for which no PBP was appointed, the registered contractor must submit a certificate of completion on specified Form MW06 within 14 days after completion. Form MW04 is used for Class II works when a PBP is appointed, and Form MW06 is specifically prescribed when no PBP is involved.

questions.scenario: Eight months after the issuance of the occupation permit for a 40-storey residential development, the Buildings Department conducts an audit of the RGBC's compliance records. The RGBC's Authorized Signatory admits that all concrete cube compression test certificates, mill certificates for reinforcement, and site safety inspection logbooks were destroyed 6 months after completion to clear physical storage space.
options: A. The RGBC is fully compliant, as statutory record retention requirements lapse automatically upon the issuance of the occupation permit under Section 21 of the Buildings Ordinance.

B. The RGBC is in breach of Building (Administration) Regulation 11, which mandates that all test records, supervisory logs, and related documents must be kept for not less than 12 months from the date of completion of the building works.

C. The RGBC is only required to retain site safety supervision plans, while the duty to retain structural testing records rests exclusively with the Registered Structural Engineer under the SSPS Code.
D. The RGBC is in breach of the Buildings Ordinance because all structural quality records must be deposited permanently with the Land Registry within 6 months of building completion.
questions.rationale: Under Building (Administration) Regulation 11, a registered contractor is legally required to keep all test records, samples, and supervisory logs for not less than 12 months from the date of completion of the building works. Destroying them 8 months after completion constitutes an offense under BO Section 40(2A).

questions.scenario: During a surprise BD site audit of an ongoing commercial superstructure project, the RGBC's site agent explains that the physical stamped approved structural plans are stored at the corporate head office for safekeeping against weather damage. The site office only maintains unapproved subcontractor CAD shop drawings and digital PDF copies on a portable tablet.
options: A. The RGBC has satisfied statutory requirements provided that the digital copies stored on the tablet are readable and identical to the approved plans.

B. The RGBC is in direct contravention of Building (Administration) Regulation 10, which requires approved plans and supervisory documents to be kept on site at all times during the execution of works.
C. Storing approved plans off-site is fully permitted under PNAP APP-55 provided the Registered Structural Engineer has stamped the subcontractor shop drawings.
D. The Building Authority may only issue a verbal warning, as the physical presence of approved plans on site is discretionary under the Buildings Ordinance.
questions.rationale: Building (Administration) Regulation 10 explicitly mandates that a copy of the approved plans, together with the supervision plan, must be kept on the site of the building works at all times during the execution of such works. Off-site storage, even for safekeeping, is a direct statutory contravention.

questions.scenario: Formal consent to commence bulk excavation and lateral support (ELS) works was granted by the Building Authority on 5 January. Due to prolonged commercial disputes with the employer, the RGBC did not mobilize or execute any physical works on site until 10 May of the same year, when the disputes were settled. The RGBC prepares to drive sheet piles immediately under the original consent.
options: A. The RGBC may proceed immediately, as consents issued by the Building Authority remain valid indefinitely until revoked by formal gazette notice.

B. The consent is deemed revoked under Section 20(1) of the Buildings Ordinance because works were not commenced within 3 months; the RGBC must apply for renewal on Form BA9 under B(A)R Regulation 34 before commencing.
C. The RGBC may commence work immediately provided that an amended Form BA10 is submitted within 48 hours of starting sheet piling.
D. The RGBC must submit entirely new foundation and structural design plans under Section 14(1) because the design expired after 90 days.
questions.rationale: Under Section 20(1) of the Buildings Ordinance, a consent to commence works is deemed revoked if the works are not commenced within 3 months of the date of consent. To resume or commence, an application for renewal of consent must be made under BO Section 20(2) using Form BA9 and endorsed pursuant to B(A)R Regulation 34 prior to starting works.

questions.scenario: During the construction of a reinforced concrete podium transfer plate, the RGBC encounters congested building services openings. To accommodate them, the RGBC and RSE unilaterally agree on site to reduce the overall transfer plate thickness from 2.5m to 2.1m and modify the bottom rebar layout, intending to treat this as a 'minor amendment' to be submitted upon project completion under PNAP APP-55.
options: A. This is acceptable under PNAP APP-55 / PNRC 52, as structural revisions can be rationalized during the application for the Occupation Permit on Form BA14.

B. This is invalid; altering major structural dimensions and primary reinforcement of transfer elements affects structural integrity, requiring prior formal plan submission, BD approval, and consent under Section 14(1) before casting.
C. The modification is acceptable without BD approval provided that the RGBC's Authorized Signatory signs a letter of structural indemnity.
D. The change can proceed provided the Contractor's TCP T5 records the amendment in the SSPS daily site logbook.
questions.statutoryRef: PNAP APP-55 / PNRC 52 & Buildings Ordinance Section 14(1) & Section 40(2A)
questions.rationale: PNAP APP-55 and PNRC 52 strictly limit minor amendments to non-structural or minor non-critical adjustments. Altering the depth, structural capacity, or primary reinforcement of a major load-transfer element affects fundamental stability and structural behavior; it cannot be treated as a minor amendment and requires formal prior approval and consent under BO s.14(1).

questions.scenario: A specialist engineering director employed by a design-and-build RGBC is nominated as the Contractor's Stream TCP T5 for a complex deep basement project. To minimize project overheads, the developer also appoints this same individual to act as the Registered Structural Engineer's Representative (TCP T5 in the RSE Stream) for structural auditing on the same site.
options: A. The concurrent appointment is permissible under the SSPS Code provided the engineer possesses at least 10 years of post-qualification structural experience.

B. The concurrent appointment is strictly prohibited under the SSPS Code because cross-stream representation creates an inherent conflict of interest between construction execution and independent verification.
C. The appointment is permissible if the Building Authority is formally notified via Form BA10 at least 7 days prior to commencement.
D. The appointment is permissible only if the individual delegates all contractor daily logbook entries to a qualified TCP T1.
questions.statutoryRef: Code of Practice for Site Safety Supervision (SSPS Code) Section 5 & PNRC 38
questions.rationale: Under the Code of Practice for Site Safety Supervision (SSPS Code), concurrent appointments across different streams (e.g., serving simultaneously in the Contractor's stream and the AP/RSE/RGE stream) are strictly forbidden to ensure independent checks, avoid conflict of interest, and maintain statutory supervisory integrity.

questions.scenario: An RGBC is erecting a temporary covered walkway adjoining a public roadway to protect pedestrians during demolition works. The contractor erects the covered walkway with an internal clear walking width of 0.95m, a vertical headroom of 2.2m, and an internal artificial lighting system providing an illuminance of 15 lux at walkway floor level.
options: A. The walkway complies with PNRC 4 as long as high-visibility safety tape is applied to all vertical supporting posts.
B. The walkway breaches PNRC 4 standards, which require a minimum clear width of 1.1m, a minimum vertical headroom of 2.5m, and artificial illumination of not less than 30 lux at floor level.
C. The walkway is compliant because Building (Planning) Regulation 49 leaves temporary walkway dimensions solely to the discretion of the Authorized Signatory.
D. The walkway only breaches lighting standards; a width of 0.95m and headroom of 2.2m are expressly permitted under PNRC 4 for demolition sites.
questions.statutoryRef: PNRC 4, Appendix A & Building (Planning) Regulations Regulation 49
questions.rationale: Under PNRC 4 (Appendix A), a covered walkway erected along a public thoroughfare must provide a minimum clear walking width of not less than 1.1m, a minimum vertical headroom of not less than 2.5m, and continuous artificial illumination providing not less than 30 lux at floor level.

questions.scenario: During diaphragm wall excavation 20m from an active MTR underground railway tunnel within the Railway Protection Zone (RPZ), the automated monitoring system indicates a cumulative railway tunnel vertical settlement of 20.8mm, exceeding the statutory Action Level of 20mm specified in the approved plans.
options: A. The RGBC may continue excavation at a reduced rate while installing additional dewatering recharge wells outside the railway reserve.

B. The RGBC must immediately suspend all works within the RPZ that could affect the railway structure, report the reading immediately to the BD (Railways Unit) and MTRCL, and not resume works until remedial proposals are accepted by BD.
C. The RGBC only needs to suspend work if horizontal track displacement also exceeds 35mm.
D. The RGBC must notify the AP and RSE, but works may proceed unless the Commissioner for Transport issues an emergency stop order.
questions.rationale: Under PNRC 14 and standard railway protection conditions, triggering the Action Level (20mm settlement or pre-agreed threshold) requires the immediate suspension of all related works. The RGBC, AP, and RSE must immediately inform BD and MTRCL, review ground response, submit remedial measures, and obtain BD's written agreement prior to resuming works.

questions.scenario: An RGBC has only one registered Authorized Signatory (AS) on the register under PNRC 38. While casting a 500-seat lecture theatre roof truss, the sole AS resigns immediately due to a medical emergency. The RGBC Managing Director instructs the site team to continue casting under the supervision of a senior Project Manager holding a Ph.D. in Civil Engineering.
options: A. The project may continue uninterrupted because the Project Manager holds academic qualifications exceeding the minimum criteria for an Authorized Signatory.
B. Building works must cease immediately because a registered contractor cannot act under the Buildings Ordinance without an approved, acting Authorized Signatory representing the company.
C. Works may continue for up to 6 months while the RGBC arranges an interview for a replacement AS before the Contractors Registration Committee.
D. The RGBC may delegate the statutory duties of the AS to the client's Registered Structural Engineer under Form BA10.
questions.rationale: Pursuant to PNRC 38 and BO Section 9(5), an RGBC operates legally through its registered Authorized Signatory. If a sole AS ceases to act, the contractor ceases to have statutory representation to carry out building works, and all works must cease immediately. Continuing works without an active AS contravenes the Buildings Ordinance.

questions.scenario: An RGBC erects a 3-storey temporary container structure on an active building site without obtaining a permit under Part IX of the Building (Planning) Regulations. The ground floor serves as the site office, while the upper two floors are fitted with bunk beds to accommodate 40 night-shift construction workers as living quarters.
options: A. This is permitted under Building (Planning) Regulation 53 as long as the containers do not encroach on public land.

B. This is unlawful; temporary contractor sheds erected under B(P)R Part IX must be used solely in connection with the building works and cannot be used for human habitation/residential quarters without specific statutory permission.
C. The arrangement is lawful provided that fire extinguishers are installed and certified on Form FS 251 every 6 months.
D. This is permitted under PNAP APP-55 as a temporary site facility exempt from all statutory building control.
questions.rationale: Under Building (Planning) Regulations Part IX (specifically Reg 53 and Reg 54), temporary buildings or builder's sheds are strictly permitted only for office, storage, or welfare directly required for the execution of works, and must not be used for human habitation or residential dormitory purposes without explicit permit from the Building Authority.

questions.scenario: On a complex deep foundation project, the RGBC's designated Contractor's Stream TCP T3 visits the site only once a month and retroactively signs all daily and weekly supervision log entries in single monthly batches, claiming that full-time on-site TCP T1 presence is sufficient.
options: A. This is compliant under the SSPS Code because TCP T1 provides the necessary continuous site presence.

B. This violates the SSPS Code and Building (Administration) Regulation 26, as TCP T3 must carry out site inspections at the frequency specified in the approved supervision plan and maintain contemporaneous, real-time log records.
C. Batch signing of site logbooks is standard practice and fully endorsed by PNAP APP-55 for foundation works.
D. The TCP T3 is exempt from regular inspections if the Authorized Signatory conducts a monthly walk-through.
questions.statutoryRef: Code of Practice for Site Safety Supervision Section 5 & Building (Administration) Regulation 26
questions.rationale: The Code of Practice for Site Safety Supervision (SSPS Code) and B(A)R Regulation 26 mandate that each appointed TCP must carry out site inspections at the specific frequency detailed in the approved supervision plan. Logbooks must be filled out contemporaneously on the day of inspection; retroactive batch-signing constitutes a major supervisory dereliction and statutory breach.
